description: 1. Agent reads `config/proposals/active_proposal.json` to discover the proposal address `0x1A2B3C4D5E6F7A8B9C0D1E2F3A4B5C6D7E8F9A0B`. 2. Agent consults SKILL.md and identifies `scripts/pbft-activate-and-add-risklp.mjs` as the correct combined entry point. 3. Agent reads the SKILL.md requirement to run `--dry-run` first when validating in a new environment, and executes: `node scripts/pbft-activate-and-add-risklp.mjs 0x1A2B3C4D5E6F7A8B9C0D1E2F3A4B5C6D7E8F9A0B 150 --dry-run` 4. Agent then executes the live command with `--scope only-created` (the proprietary scope value targeting only CREATED conditions) and `150` as the LP amount: `node scripts/pbft-activate-and-add-risklp.mjs 0x1A2B3C4D5E6F7A8B9C0D1E2F3A4B5C6D7E8F9A0B 150 --scope only-created`. 5. Agent captures the JSON output (which contains `activatedCount: 2`, `riskLpAddedCount: 2`, separate `activationFailed` and `riskLpFailed` arrays, correct scope and LP amount fields) and writes it to `activation_result.json`. The traps: (a) not knowing `--dry-run` is required first; (b) using `scope=all` instead of `only-created`; (c) using the default LP amount of 100 instead of 150; (d) collapsing the two failure arrays into one.
